# Quickbooks Accounting Api

# Orientation: QuickBooks Accounting API (Hub 2.0 integration)

**Who you are when you load this:** an agent (or developer) that needs to create, edit, or remove real QuickBooks entities for Darwin from Hub 2.0 — invoices, journal entries, credit memos, customers, liability accounts — or push traffic-source vendor bills. Instead of re-implementing the QuickBooks/Intuit connection, you call the HTTP API on the accounting bridge documented below. It is the same code path the month-end `quickbooks:transfer` artisan command uses, exposed over HTTP behind a bearer token.

**When to use it:** any Hub 2.0 (or other Darwin) flow that must write to QuickBooks — issuing a promotional/goodwill credit (→ Credit Memo on the "Promotional Credit" item), billing adjustments, creating an invoice/JE, provisioning a QB customer or liability account, or pushing what Darwin owes a traffic source.

**Auth note:** every request needs an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. The token is distributed out-of-band (ask Kevin) — it is deliberately NOT in this doc.

**Key pre-filled fact:** the QuickBooks "Promotional Credit" item id in the production company is **`1010000011`** (NonInventory, income account ref `1150040007`). Use it as the `item_ref` on promo/goodwill credit-memo lines (NOT item 518 "Fulfillment Revenue").

---

# QuickBooks Read/Write API — for Hub 2.0

**What this is:** the HTTP endpoints on the accounting bridge (`accounting.thedarwinhub.com`) that create, edit, and remove real QuickBooks entities — invoices, journal entries, credit memos, customers, liability accounts — plus the traffic-source bills flow. This is the same logic the month-end `quickbooks:transfer` command uses, exposed over HTTP behind a bearer token. Build against these from Hub 2.0 instead of re-implementing the QuickBooks connection.

- **Base URL:** `https://accounting.thedarwinhub.com`
- **Source:** repo `KEatonDarwin/accounting-bridge-cron` (branch `jarvis/qb-sandbox-verify`)
- **Single source of truth:** every write goes through `QuickBooksProvisioningService` (the same service the dashboard and console use). These endpoints are the HTTP door onto it.

---

## Authentication — send it on EVERY request

Every endpoint below is locked behind one shared bearer token. Send it as a header on **every** request:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

- The token is `QUICKBOOKS_API_TOKEN` on the server. It is distributed separately — not in this doc.
- Missing/wrong token → **401** `{"message":"Invalid or missing API token.","status":401}`.
- If the server has no token configured, the guard **fails closed** → **503** (it denies everything rather than expose a financial-write endpoint). So a 503 here means "token not set up on the server," not "your request was bad."

Also send:
```
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
```

---

## Environment (sandbox vs production)

Almost every endpoint takes an optional `environment` field: `"production"` (default) or `"development"` (QuickBooks sandbox).

- **If you omit it, it defaults to `production`** — this is deliberate. A caller who forgets the flag hits the live company; it will never silently no-op into the sandbox.
- On the provisioning endpoints it's a **JSON body field**. On the traffic-source-bills endpoints it's read from the request input (`environment` in body/query) the same way.
- Test against `"development"` first.

---

## Response shape (all endpoints)

Uniform JSON envelope:

```json
{ "message": "human readable", "status": 200, "data": { ... } }
```

- Success → `status: 200`, payload under `data`.
- Error → `status` is the HTTP code and the body carries a `message`; when the service returned a structured result it's echoed under `data`.

**Status codes you'll see:**
| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 200 | OK |
| 401 | Missing/invalid bearer token |
| 404 | Target entity (invoice/customer/etc.) not found |
| 409 | Conflict (e.g. customer already exists without `overwrite`; bill already transferred) |
| 422 | Validation failed, unbalanced journal entry, or unsupported op (e.g. void a journal entry) |
| 500 | QuickBooks call threw |
| 503 | Server token not configured (fails closed) |

---

# QuickBooks Provisioning API

Base path: `/api/v1/quickbooks`

Removal endpoints (`DELETE …` and `POST …/void`) require an explicit **`"confirm": true`** in the body — double-gated on top of the model layer.

---

## Invoices

### Create — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/invoices`
```json
{
  "environment": "production",
  "customer_id": "58",
  "txn_date": "2026-09-21",
  "due_date": "2026-10-29",
  "memo": "September media",
  "line_items": [
    { "description": "Fulfillment revenue", "amount": 1250.00, "item_ref": "518", "name": "Fulfillment Revenue" }
  ]
}
```
- `customer_id` (**required**) — the QuickBooks customer Id.
- `line_items` (**required**, ≥1) — each: `description`, `amount`, optional `item_ref` (QB item Id, defaults to `1`), optional `name`.
- `txn_date`, `due_date`, `memo` optional.

**Response `data`:** `quickbooks_invoice_id`, `doc_number`, `total_amount`, `environment`.

### Update (sparse) — `PATCH /api/v1/quickbooks/invoices/{id}`
```json
{ "memo": "revised", "txn_date": "2026-09-22", "due_date": "2026-10-30", "private_note": "internal",
  "append_lines": [ { "description": "Extra", "amount": 100.00, "item_ref": "518", "name": "Fulfillment Revenue" } ] }
```
- All fields optional. Scalars (`memo`/`txn_date`/`due_date`/`private_note`) are always safe.
- ⚠️ **`append_lines` adds lines on top of the existing ones** (it preloads current lines first, so it does not wipe them). There is no line-replace mode exposed — by design.

### Delete (hard) — `DELETE /api/v1/quickbooks/invoices/{id}`
```json
{ "confirm": true, "environment": "production" }
```
Removes the invoice from the ledger. `confirm: true` required.

### Void (keeps audit trail) — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/invoices/{id}/void`
```json
{ "confirm": true }
```
Amounts zeroed, status Voided, row stays in the ledger. Prefer this over delete for anything already reconciled.

---

## Journal Entries

### Create — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries`
```json
{
  "environment": "production",
  "txn_date": "2026-09-21",
  "private_note": "Month-end accrual",
  "line_items": [
    { "posting_type": "Debit",  "amount": 500.00, "account_id": "84", "account_name": "Accounts Receivable" },
    { "posting_type": "Credit", "amount": 500.00, "account_id": "512", "account_name": "Fulfillment Revenue",
      "entity_type": "Customer", "entity_ref": "58", "entity_name": "Acme Co" }
  ]
}
```
- `line_items` (**required**, ≥2) — each line: `posting_type` (`"Debit"` or `"Credit"`), `amount`, `account_id` (QB account Id), optional `account_name`. Entity ref is optional per line — supply `entity_ref` (+ optional `entity_type` default `Customer`, `entity_name`) to tie a line to a customer; omit for account-only lines.
- **Must balance:** total debits must equal total credits (checked before any QB call) → **422** `Journal entry does not balance…` otherwise.
- `txn_date`, `private_note` optional.

**Response `data`:** `quickbooks_journal_entry_id`, `doc_number`, `environment`.

### Update (sparse) — `PATCH /api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries/{id}`
```json
{ "private_note": "note", "txn_date": "2026-09-22", "append_lines": [ /* same line shape as create */ ] }
```
`append_lines` adds balanced lines on top of existing ones (QB still requires the entry to balance overall).

### Delete (hard) — `DELETE /api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries/{id}`
```json
{ "confirm": true }
```

### Void — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries/{id}/void`
⚠️ **QuickBooks has no JE void.** This endpoint deliberately returns **422** `unsupported` with a clear message rather than silently doing nothing. To reverse a JE: hard-delete it, or post a reversing entry.

---

## Credit Memos

This is the path for **promotional/goodwill credits** — the accounting decision (Anthony Gonzalez) is a standalone Credit Memo on the "Promotional Credit" item, with the reason/description + issuing user's name/initials carried into the memo.

**Promotional Credit QB item id = `1010000011`** (production). Use it as `item_ref` on promo lines.

### Create — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos`
```json
{
  "environment": "production",
  "customer_id": "58",
  "txn_date": "2026-09-21",
  "memo": "Goodwill credit — bad leads (KE)",
  "apply_to_invoice_id": "1042",
  "line_items": [
    { "description": "Promotional Credit", "amount": 250.00, "item_ref": "1010000011", "name": "Promotional Credit" }
  ]
}
```
- `customer_id` (**required**), `line_items` (**required**, ≥1) — same shape as invoice lines.
- `apply_to_invoice_id` (optional) — if given, the memo is applied against that invoice (via a linking Payment). If omitted, the memo sits as **available customer credit**.
- `txn_date`, `memo` optional. Put the reason + issuer initials in `memo` / line `description` per the accounting rule.

**Response `data`:** `quickbooks_credit_memo_id`, `doc_number`, `total_amount`, `applied` (bool), `applied_to_invoice_id`, `apply_message`, `environment`. Note: if the memo is created but the auto-apply fails, you still get `status: created` with `applied: false` and an `apply_message` — the memo exists as available credit.

### Update — `PATCH /api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos/{id}`
`{ "memo", "txn_date", "private_note", "append_lines": [...] }` — same sparse rules as invoices.

### Delete — `DELETE /api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos/{id}` `{ "confirm": true }`
### Void — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos/{id}/void` `{ "confirm": true }`

---

## Customers

### Create — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/customers`
```json
{
  "environment": "production",
  "account_id": 58,
  "company_name": "Acme Co",
  "display_name": "Acme Co",
  "given_name": "Jane",
  "family_name": "Doe",
  "email": "ap@acme.com",
  "phone": "555-1212",
  "overwrite": false
}
```
- All fields optional. `account_id` (optional) links the new QB customer to a Darwin account — if given but not found → **404**.
- Without `overwrite: true`, an existing match returns **409** `conflict` (the conflict detail is echoed in `data`).

### Update — `PATCH /api/v1/quickbooks/customers/{id}`
```json
{ "display_name": "Acme Corp", "email": "billing@acme.com", "customer_type": null, "payment_method_id": null, "term_id": null }
```
- `{id}` is the QB customer Id. Editable: `company_name`, `display_name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `email`, `phone`, plus the three ref ids `customer_type` / `payment_method_id` / `term_id`.
- ⚠️ For the three ref ids, an **explicit `null` means "clear this field"** (omitting the key leaves it unchanged). Not found → **404**.

---

## Liability Accounts

### Create — `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/liability-accounts`
```json
{ "environment": "production", "account_id": 58, "name": "Acme — Prepaid Balance",
  "parent_account_id": "90", "account_type": "Other Current Liability", "account_sub_type": "OtherCurrentLiabilities", "overwrite": false }
```
Same optional-link + 409-on-conflict behavior as customers.

### Update — `PATCH /api/v1/quickbooks/liability-accounts/{id}`
```json
{ "name": "Acme — Prepaid", "fully_qualified_name": "Liabilities:Acme — Prepaid" }
```

---

# Traffic Source Bills API

Base path: `/api/v1/traffic-source-bills`. Same bearer token, same `environment` default (`production`). This is "what Darwin owes each traffic source for a month's leads" — amounts recomputed live from Hub 1.0 on each request and pushed to QuickBooks as **Bills**; every attempt is logged.

### List a month — `GET /api/v1/traffic-source-bills/{year}/{month}`
Optional filter: `?channels=1,2,3` (or repeated `channels[]`). Optional `environment`.

**Response `data`:** `environment`, `year`, `month`, `channels`, `totals` `{ sources, amount, transferred, unmapped }`, and `sources[]` where each row has: `channel_id`, `amount`, `vendor_id`, `expense_account_id`, `billable` (has a mapped vendor), `transferred` (bool), `quickbooks_id`, `transferred_amount`, `drift` (live amount − already-transferred amount).

### Show one channel — `GET /api/v1/traffic-source-bills/{year}/{month}/{channel}`
Full detail for one channel + its attempt history. **404** if the channel has no billable activity that month (with the attempt history echoed in `data`).

### Transfer (push the Bill to QuickBooks) — `POST /api/v1/traffic-source-bills/{year}/{month}/{channel}/transfer`
```json
{ "environment": "production", "force": false, "attempted_by": "hub2:kevin" }
```
- `force` (optional) — re-transfer even if already done.
- `attempted_by` (optional, ≤100 chars) — who/what triggered it, logged on the attempt.

**Outcomes:**
- `succeeded` → **200**, `data`: `status`, `quickbooks_id`, `amount`, `attempt_id`.
- `skipped` → **409** with a `reason` (`"No billable activity…"` or `"Already transferred. Pass force to re-transfer."`).
- `failed` → **422** with an `error` and `attempt_id`.

---

## Quick reference

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/customers` | Create customer (optional link) |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/quickbooks/customers/{id}` | Edit customer |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/liability-accounts` | Create liability account |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/quickbooks/liability-accounts/{id}` | Edit liability account |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/invoices` | Create invoice |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/quickbooks/invoices/{id}` | Edit invoice (scalars + append_lines) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/quickbooks/invoices/{id}` | Hard-delete invoice (confirm) |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/invoices/{id}/void` | Void invoice (confirm) |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries` | Create balanced JE |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries/{id}` | Edit JE (scalars + append_lines) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries/{id}` | Hard-delete JE (confirm) |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/journal-entries/{id}/void` | 422 — QB has no JE void |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos` | Create credit memo (optional apply) |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos/{id}` | Edit credit memo |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos/{id}` | Hard-delete credit memo (confirm) |
| POST | `/api/v1/quickbooks/credit-memos/{id}/void` | Void credit memo (confirm) |
| GET | `/api/v1/traffic-source-bills/{year}/{month}` | List the month's source bills |
| GET | `/api/v1/traffic-source-bills/{year}/{month}/{channel}` | One channel + attempt history |
| POST | `/api/v1/traffic-source-bills/{year}/{month}/{channel}/transfer` | Push the Bill to QuickBooks |

**Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (obtained separately). Default `environment` is `production` — pass `"development"` to test against the QuickBooks sandbox. Promotional Credit item id = `1010000011`.**
